stories.headline: Union rallies behind Merz as 'Kanzlertausch' speculation dominates German politics
stories.summary: Reports emerged that some CDU/CSU figures had been contemplating replacing Chancellor Friedrich Merz with NRW Minister-President Hendrik Wüst, triggering a week-long political crisis. Leading CDU and CSU politicians — including Wüst himself, Spahn, Rhein, Linnemann, Weber, and Günther — publicly declared support for Merz, with the two men set to meet at a closed CDU caucus in Meschede/Sauerland on Monday. Polls showed Merz at a historic low of 83% disapproval, and coalition performance at only 34%.

stories.headline: Pistorius lobbies Canada for multi-billion TKMS submarine contract in Ottawa visit
stories.summary: Defense Minister Boris Pistorius traveled to Canada to advocate for a German-Norwegian TKMS submarine deal (12 boats, potentially billions of euros), visiting the CANSEC defense fair and signing a memorandum of understanding with Canadian firm CAE. Germany competes against South Korea; Canada is expected to decide by end of June. Pistorius also called for deeper strategic partnership with Canada as US reliability as ally declines. A planned US leg of the trip was cancelled after Pentagon chief Hegseth had no available meeting time.

stories.headline: Pistorius proposes mandatory reserve training obligations for Bundeswehr veterans
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pistorius announced a draft 'Reservestärkungsgesetz' that would end the 'double voluntariness' principle and allow the state to compel former soldiers to participate in peacetime reserve exercises. Employers would be required to release reservist employees up to a set limit. The Reservistenverband welcomed the plan; employers' associations objected. The goal is to build a 200,000-strong reserve to complement 260,000 active troops.

He awarded the Hambacher Freiheitspreis 1832 to Polish constitutional scholar and former justice minister Adam Bodnar. Wadephul described Germany as a reliable mediator and rules-based actor. The vote is scheduled for Wednesday, June 3; German officials described it as a close race and not a foregone conclusion.

stories.headline: German government condemns Russian drone strike on Romanian city of Galati
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential building in Galati, Romania — the first such hit on a densely populated NATO area since the start of the war. Chancellor Merz condemned the incident as demonstrating Russia's willingness to escalate and called for a stronger NATO eastern flank. Foreign Minister Wadephul announced a coordinated NATO/EU response and demanded greater investment in air defense. Romania's general staff did not classify it as a deliberate targeted attack.

stories.headline: Germany's May inflation drops to 2.6% as government fuel tax rebate takes effect
stories.summary: Germany's consumer price inflation fell unexpectedly from 2.9% in April to 2.6% in May, driven mainly by the government's fuel price subsidy (Tankrabatt). The Bundesbank had previously estimated the measure would reduce inflation by roughly a quarter percentage point in May and June. The bank warned that the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruptions could push rates back up in coming months.

stories.headline: Klingbeil hosts E6 finance ministers summit on EU capital markets union
stories.summary: Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil hosted finance ministers from France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, and Spain at the Bundesbank guesthouse in Berlin to advance the stalled EU capital markets union. Klingbeil criticized Europe's 'snail's pace' and called for accelerated reform. Ministers agreed in principle on a phased expansion of European supervisory authority over financial markets, crypto, and market infrastructure.

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wadephul expressed concern about Israeli military advances in southern Lebanon, calling on both Israel and Hezbollah to return to the agreed ceasefire. Wadephul said Israel has legitimate security interests but warned that further escalation causes civilian displacement and risks making parts of Lebanon permanently uninhabitable. He made the statements from New York during his UN Security Council lobbying trip.

stories.summary: Wolfgang Kubicki was elected the new FDP party leader, succeeding Christian Dürr. Kubicki rejected the party's 'firewall' against the AfD in parliamentary procedure matters, though ruled out coalition partnerships. Outgoing FDP figures used the party congress to attack the Merz government for what they called excessive debt accumulation and failed economic reform. FDP remains below the 5% Bundestag threshold in polls.

stories.headline: US reduces NATO contributions; German coalition debates European defense gap
stories.summary: Following the NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, reports emerged that the US is making substantial cuts to its NATO military commitments — including bombers, submarines, and surveillance drones — that Europeans had not anticipated. German CDU politicians demanded Pistorius present a concept for filling the gap; the Wehrbeauftragter called for planning certainty. Five NATO states, including the UK, also rejected Wadephul's proposal for additional Ukraine military aid beyond the existing EU credit.

stories.headline: Canada-Germany LNG export deal signed for Ksi Lisims Pacific terminal
stories.summary: Canada and Germany signed an agreement for the export of one million tonnes of liquefied natural gas per year from the proposed Ksi Lisims terminal on British Columbia's coast to Germany's SEFE (Securing Energy for Europe) group, with deliveries expected in the early 2030s. The deal, announced alongside Prime Minister Carney's push to diversify from US markets, would represent Canada's first long-term LNG exports to Europe.

stories.headline: Bundeswehr deploys to Lithuania for NATO 'Freedom Shield' exercise; German-Dutch corps takes on Baltic role
stories.summary: The Bundeswehr deployed 2,300 troops, Leopard 2 tanks, and Puma infantry fighting vehicles to Lithuania for the NATO 'Freedom Shield' exercise. Separately, the 1st German-Dutch Corps in Münster is set to formally take over additional NATO responsibilities at the Baltic eastern flank from mid-year, assuming responsibility from the Multinational Corps Northeast in Stettin. Germany, with Pistorius present, also endorsed plans for a new NATO corps structure covering the Baltics.

stories.headline: Bundeswehr discharges 19 soldiers under new law removing extremists from service
stories.summary: The German government confirmed that 19 Bundeswehr members had been discharged under an accelerated dismissal law for 'constitutionally hostile' soldiers, originally passed by the coalition government. The figure emerged in response to a parliamentary query from the AfD. The Military Counter-Intelligence Service (MAD) oversees such cases.

stories.headline: Wadephul pushes additional Ukraine military funding and proposes NATO supplementary contributions
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Wadephul proposed at the NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg that allies add bilateral military contributions on top of the existing EU credit for Ukraine, citing a 40% gap in Ukrainian weapons production funding. The proposal met mixed reception; the AfD and Germany's right-wing press criticized it as reckless spending. Separately, Wadephul's Auswärtiges Amt maintained a cautious line on EU-Turkey relations despite Turkish crackdowns on the CHP opposition.

stories.headline: Bundesbank halts Frankfurt HQ renovation; 100 specially hired building specialists left without work
stories.summary: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel cancelled the billion-euro renovation of the central bank's legendary Frankfurt headquarters, leaving approximately 100 building specialists hired specifically for the project without assigned tasks. Their status is unclear. The decision appeared to reverse months of planning and raises management accountability questions at the institution.

stories.headline: Pistorius defense ministry criticized for excessive secrecy classifications on arms procurement
stories.summary: Wirtschaftswoche reported that MPs and defense experts are complaining of 'classification inflation' at the defense ministry under Pistorius, with a massive increase in the number of documents classified as secret. Multiple sources independently described the trend as creating parliamentary oversight problems and industry uncertainty.

stories.headline: BND undergoing major reform as new director Jaeger overhauls structure; Russia phishing campaign targets German officials
stories.summary: Germany's foreign intelligence service BND is undergoing wide-reaching organizational reform under new director Martin Jaeger, who took over in September 2025. Staff resentment over opaque promotions has emerged. Separately, a Russian state-linked phishing campaign using Signal QR-code links has targeted German politicians, senior military officers, diplomats, and journalists, with BND vice president Arndt Freytag von Loringhoven among confirmed victims.
